newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - June T-bond downtrend poised to resume.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - June T-bond downtrend poised to resume.

text.p: Next week's busy economic calendar could provide the spark for a resumption of the months-long downtrend in June U.S. Treasury bond futures, analysts said.

Any one in the series of important numbers due out, beginning with Tuesday's first-quarter employment cost index and ending with April employment data on May 2, could serve as the agent for fresh lows and new yield highs on the long bond, said Steven Poser, senior technical analyst for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"It's hard to be bullish here," Poser said. June Treasury bond futures this morning edged briefly into the upper 106-00 handle, extending a near-term slump that began midweek.
The contract was last trading at 107-08, down 2/32. Bond futures appear to be headed for more consolidation in the rest of the session, said Donald Pullen, floor analyst for E.D. and F. Man.
Pullen targeted key support at 106-29, the April 16 low made on stronger than expected March industrial production and capacity utilization figures, followed by 106-20.
Poser said he expected the 106-29 level to hold, with next support coming in at 106-27, an intraday Elliott Wave target.
"I don't think it's going to collapse, at least not today," he said.

However, he looked for June to visit the 105-00 handle sometime next week on its way to upper-104 levels, the final leg lower in a five-wave pattern. Along the way, the market could extend the upper-range barrier to 107-18, which should be viewed as a selling opportunity, he said.
The analysts stressed the importance of next week's economic lineup to price direction.
"Technically, I think the market at this point remains on the defense," Pullen said. But more importantly, he said, "the market's going to be driven by the fundamentals next week."
The data will help solidify market opinion in the debate over whether the Federal Reserve will tighten credit again in May, Pullen said.
